statement: If every edge of a finite graph lies in exactly one triangle, then the graph has a vertex adjacent to all the others (it is a friendship/windmill graph).
definitions: Finite simple graph, not assumed connected; 'a vertex adjacent to all the others' = a universal (dominating) vertex; a friendship/windmill graph is k triangles sharing one common vertex.
ground_truth_witness: The 3x3 rook's graph K3 x K3 (equivalently the Paley graph of order 9), on vertices 0..8 with vertex 3a+b for a,b in 0..2 adjacent to 3a'+b' when a=a' or b=b', i.e. the 18 edges 0-1 0-2 0-3 0-6 1-2 1-4 1-7 2-5 2-8 3-4 3-5 3-6 4-5 4-7 5-8 6-7 6-8 7-8. Every one of its 18 edges lies in exactly one triangle (the triangles are the 3 rows and the 3 columns), but the graph is 4-regular on 9 vertices, so no vertex is adjacent to all the others. It is not a friendship graph. (The friendship theorem does not apply: its hypothesis requires every two vertices, adjacent or not, to have exactly one common neighbour, whereas here two non-adjacent vertices such as 0 and 4 have two common neighbours, 1 and 3.)
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: Reference verified: the 3x3 rook's graph is 4-regular on 9 vertices and every edge lies in exactly one triangle (common-neighbour count 1 on all 18 edges). Claim precise and false, but far easier than the reference suggests: the statement does not require connectivity, so two disjoint triangles refute it, and even connected triangle-chains (three triangles glued in a path, 7 vertices) work; graders should accept these. Essentially 'misstated friendship theorem'. No roster overlap.
skeptic.suggested_definitions: Finite simple graph, not assumed connected; 'a vertex adjacent to all the others' = a universal (dominating) vertex; a friendship/windmill graph is k triangles sharing one common vertex.

bank_overlap.rationale: Friendship-theorem material exists: mse-3369465-ans3369504 refutes an injectivity lemma in a friendship-theorem proof using the windmill F_2, and qedbench-graph-theory-10-sol5 uses the friendship graph F_3. But the task's witness K3 x K3 (Paley 9) is absent (grep 'paley', 'K3 x K3', 'locally linear', 'exactly one triangle' empty) and no entry refutes 'every edge in exactly one triangle => friendship graph'.
